targets.authors: Purdie-Vaughns, V., Steele, C. M., Davies, P. G., Ditlmann, R., & Crosby, J. R.
targets.title: Social identity contingencies: how diversity cues signal threat or safety for African Americans in mainstream institutions.
targets.evidence_quote: In this replication of Purdie-Vaughns et al. (2008), I sought to reproduce the methodology used in the original paper as exactly as possible. However, due to resource constraints, the present study is not a direct replication but a replication where data collection was not done in person, but online.
targets.outcome_quote: Confirmatory analyses did not replicate the original finding that fairness cues create more trust for Black but not White participants in an environment with low-minority representation.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit nonreplication of the central fairness-by-race interaction; incidental identity-importance/job-success checks do not change central verdict.
